cells.tense: You are building the thing and you are still in the room with the people in it.
cells.ask: Before the next change settles, ask one person how it lands for them. Nothing more. Do it while it's still yours to adjust.
cells.core:
You're moving something into a shape it can hold, slowly, and the people close to you are inside that change rather than downstream of it. You can hear a correction without treating it as a verdict, which is why the thing keeps getting built and the closeness survives it.

What's good here is that the building and the people connect instead of competing — ask, adjust, keep talking. Solo time is where you sharpen, not where you hide, and it comes back into the room with you. Keeping this costs you something: the asking keeps going, even on days you'd rather just decide. The practice isn't the building. It's staying in contact while the building happens.
cells.sheetLine: You build the change and stay in touch with the people in it.
cells.verb: forcing change into a shape that can hold
cells.place: in the connection between you and the people near you

cells.tense: You are bracing for a shape that is not finished and pushing people toward it anyway.
cells.ask: Say one thing that is still unfinished out loud to someone, and ask them to talk about it with you instead of agreeing with it.
cells.core:
You're pushing a change into form ahead of when it can hold, and the people nearest you are paying for it. They say something about how it's going and you hear the fix they're missing. So you explain more, more exactly, and the explaining has become the way you're together.

That's what has crowded the relating out. You might say nobody's keeping up, and what's true is nobody's been let in before the version was locked. What gets cut first is the talking that can't be converted into progress.

So start there: let one thing stay open where someone can answer into it. Not a report, not a decision, something still soft. You'll know the push is off when the answer changes the plan.

cells.tense: You stopped putting your weight into what you see, and that froze the room, not just the work.
cells.ask: State one position on something in front of one person, in a plain sentence, no hedging, and let it stand even if it's wrong.
cells.core:
Something you saw clearly hasn't gone anywhere. The moving of it did. So the room keeps drifting and you keep adjusting to it, and the closeness you have with people is mostly agreeing with them.

What's absent isn't feeling — you feel plenty. It's putting a stake down where someone can see it and disagree. That's what lets people settle around you instead of waiting for a cue.

Pick one thing, in front of one person, and say the position plainly. No cushion, no maybe, no roundabout. If it lands wrong, that's information. The point tonight is only that you said it where someone could hear it and stay.
cells.sheetLine: You see it clearly but you've stopped saying where you stand.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what happens between people here, while talking about it as if it happens on its own.
cells.ask: Tell one person plainly what you did to bring them into this thing. Two sentences. Then stop and let them say what it was like from their side.
cells.core:
Think about the last thing you organized and who got included because you decided it. You selected, you invited, you set what was fair. You describe those as just how it went — nobody chose that, it's just the way it turned out.

Your own name stays out of the sentence. The motion is real; things change because you're moving them. Only the credit is unplaced.

What's held back costs you too. People can't meet someone who keeps insisting the current moved them. So name one thing you did and let someone tell you what it was like — not to be thanked, just to be seen where you already stand.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering this and still calling it the way things went.
